reason: This passage (Exodus 19) describes the preparation for the covenant at Mount Sinai, with Yahweh instructing Moses to sanctify the people and establish boundaries around the mountain. The text contains no complaints, murmuring, or expressions of ingratitude from the Hebrews toward either their leaders (Moses) or Yahweh. Instead, the people are shown following the prescribed preparations—sanctifying themselves, washing their clothes, and preparing to meet Yahweh. Moses acts as a faithful mediator, and the focus of the narrative is on obedience and reverence, not on ingratitude.
